title: Data Quality and Leakage Prevention
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of data quality and leakage prevention in a PyTorch workflow.
Apply a small example of data quality and leakage prevention and interpret the output.
Identify a relevant limitation, debugging check, or reproducibility concern.

content.intro: Data Quality and Leakage Prevention: A Dataset describes how to retrieve one sample, while a DataLoader groups samples into batches and controls ordering, worker processes, and collation. In this lesson, use a small example to make the inputs, outputs, and boundary conditions explicit.
content.why_it_matters: A dependable data pipeline makes training repeatable and prevents shape, label, leakage, and throughput problems from being mistaken for model problems. For this lesson, focus on missing or corrupted samples and the evidence you can collect from a controlled example.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Keep sample retrieval separate from batching and transforms. Split data before fitting preprocessing, and ensure train/validation/inference transformations are appropriate to each stage. The source topics for this lesson are: Missing or corrupted samples, Label validation, Duplicate detection. Keep each topic connected to a checkable input/output behavior.

content_blocks.title: Read the example
content_blocks.text: Inspect one dataset item, one batched output, and the feature/label shapes. Use num_workers=0 while debugging custom datasets. The example is a teaching-scale check, not evidence of a trained model score or a hardware-independent performance claim.

content.task: Try it yourself: Build a tiny custom Dataset returning a feature and label, inspect one item, and iterate it in batches with DataLoader. Record the observed result and one limitation; do not report an unrun training or performance result as measured.
task_acceptance_criteria: The experiment demonstrates at least one relevant aspect of data quality and leakage prevention.
Record the expected and observed result, including shape/dtype/device information when relevant.
Explain one common failure mode, compatibility limitation, or evaluation caveat.

troubleshooting.symptom: A tensor operation raises a shape, dtype, or device mismatch.
troubleshooting.check: Print .shape, .dtype, and .device for each input. Resolve the mismatch intentionally instead of changing dimensions blindly.

troubleshooting.symptom: The example fails because an optional package or accelerator is unavailable.
troubleshooting.check: Check the installed PyTorch/package versions and device availability. Use the official installation selector and run the CPU-compatible path where appropriate.

troubleshooting.symptom: The result differs across runs or machines.
troubleshooting.check: Fix the seed where useful, record versions and inputs, and document operations that remain nondeterministic or hardware dependent.

common_mistakes.problem: Relying on assumptions instead of inspecting the data or output.
common_mistakes.why: Many ML failures come from incorrect shapes, labels, preprocessing, or execution mode rather than a syntax error.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect representative inputs and add assertions for the expected shape, dtype, range, or behavior.

common_mistakes.problem: Mixing training-time behavior with inference-time behavior.
common_mistakes.why: Dropout, normalization, gradient tracking, and optimizer updates can change how a model behaves.
common_mistakes.fix: Do not shuffle or split features and labels independently; their indices must remain aligned.

common_mistakes.problem: Using a current or experimental API without recording its version assumptions.
common_mistakes.why: Hardware support and ecosystem APIs can change independently of the core package.
common_mistakes.fix: Pin compatible dependencies, record the environment, and test after upgrades.
